summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 3.1/28)

data.turoyo: Kule mi zuḥṯayḏan, mzarṭinawo b ruḥayna mi zuḥṯayḏan.
data.translation: Das alles (sagten wir) aus Angst, wir stießen von uns aus Drohungen aus, vor lauter Angst.

rationale: First Infectum-wa box: first-person plural, fear as cause and b ruḥayna.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 3.2/15)

data.turoyo: Mzarṭiwo, əmmiwo: "Kaṯi..." mede ḥreno l əḏʕiwo mad duwal aǧnabiye, Turkiya, u dušman diḏa Ruṣya yo, həne mafəḥiwa lebayye, əmmiwa: "Kaṯi u Ruṣ laff elayna."
data.translation: Sie drohten ihnen, sie sagten: Jetzt kommt ... sie kannten keinen anderen von den ausländischen Staaten, (sie wussten nur), dass der Feind der Türkei Russland war. So machten sie sich selber Mut und sagten: Jetzt kommt Russland uns (zu Hilfe).

rationale: New Infectum-wa box: third-person plural and explicit bravado content.

data.turoyo: Komər məlle: "Zərṭat zoyəd me ruḥux lo mzarṭat! W hayo, raḥuqo yo ste menux, d qədrat saymat mede ebi!"
data.translation: Muhammed sprach: Laß das überflüssige Geprahle! du kannst mir noch lange nichts anhaben. -

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: prohibitive lo with cognate plural Zərṭat, not an Imperativ.

summary: New idiom: mzaraṭle/mzarəṭ zərṭat (ʕal) 'Drohungen, Prahlreden ausstoßen'

data.turoyo: mḥeleli u=mede d aṯi mine, ono-ste mzaraṭli aʕle zərṭat d rab mam=məḥwoṯe.
data.translation: Er schlug mich, was er nur konnte, und ich schleuderte ihm Drohungen entgegen, die stärker waren als die Schläge.

rationale: Recurrent cognate-noun collocation, also in 69/545 and113/79; read-only zərṭ search found no existing listing. Not a new numbered meaning or literal throwing verb.

summary: The input has four II Preterit examples, including the MAC Dawid quotation; several reader thin-cell counts of three are stale. Infectum has one, and Infectum-wa was absent.
Targets take ʕal-/aʕle, or a delayed shared NP with hdd in40/15. The driver is understood from the preceding speech phrase in Talay1/32.
zərṭat/zərṭayo supply a cognate noun with the fully inflected borrowed verb. The construction is indexed as a collocation, not a new sense; German schleuderte does not establish throwing.
b ruḥe/b ruḥayna and l ruḥe occur with boasting. They may express self-generated bluster rather than literal self-address; no independent semantic division is established.
Kurdish zirt dan is inherited etymological information. These tokens show Turoyo II morphology but do not alone establish a contact history or syntactic calque.
Taunting before a charge, menacing an opponent, scolding and rallying companions all fit the broad inherited gloss. No Detransitive evidence.
What is the precise difference between b ruḥe in65/449 and b ruḥayna inJTM3.1/28, versus l ruḥe in65/370: self-address, spontaneous bluster, or emphasis?
Do speakers regard zrṭ with zərṭat as a regular cognate object or a fixed contact-influenced collocation? The recurrent form is documented without choosing a contact derivation.
